subject: SLA construct, multi-year discount & on-call scope
messages:
From: Ari Glass <ari@signalops.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: SLA construct & pricing ask (SignalOps)

Diego / team,

Thanks for taking a look at SignalOps' support needs. We're finalizing our vendor shortlist and I wanted a clear, scannable view of how Redwood would package:

- Uptime tiers (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) and corresponding credit schedules
- Response SLAs for P1/P2 (acknowledge / TTR expectations)
- Escalation coverage (on-call windows, overlap with our team, weekend support)
- Pricing for a 36-month commit vs 12-month, and what discounts/credits are standard vs negotiable

Attached is a short requirements note (SignalOps-requirements-20280306.pdf). Our procurement timeline is tight: internal approvals by 3/15 and PO soon after.

Can you send a one-pager that maps tiers -> deliverables -> price bands? If possible, include a sample mutual action plan we could attach to the SOW.

Regards,
Ari Glass
Head of Platform Reliability, SignalOps
ari@signalops.com
+1 415-555-0124

Attachments: SignalOps-requirements-20280306.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Glass <ari@signalops.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA construct & pricing ask (SignalOps)

Hi Ari — thanks for the clear brief and the timeline.

Quick summary below; attaching a formatted SKU matrix and a short mutual action plan for procurement. High level options:

1) Baseline (Standard) — 99.9% uptime, P1 ack within 30 min (business-hours), P1 TTR target 6 hours, business-hours on-call (M-F).
   - Use case: non-critical production workloads
   - Pricing: Consumption + $X/mo support retainer

2) Preferred (Enhanced) — 99.95% uptime, P1 ack 15 min, P1 TTR target 3 hours, extended on-call 8x5 with on-call handoff overlap.
   - Use case: customer-facing inference; moderate risk
   - Pricing: higher retainer + reduced per-token priority surcharge

3) Assured (Premium) — 99.99% uptime, P1 ack 5 min, P1 TTR target 60–120 min, 24x7 on-call with named escalation contacts and guaranteed response tiers.
   - Use case: safety/financial/regulatory-critical systems
   - Pricing: committed capacity + premium retainer; SLA credits escalate with severity.

Discounting guidance for multi-year commits (36 months):
- Standard: 8–12% off list for 36m committed spend versus 12m
- Preferred: 10–15% for 36m, plus one-time onboarding credit applied in first quarter
- Assured: 12–18% for 36m depending on commit level and payment terms; larger credits available if Redwood-managed private deployment required

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan excerpt in attached PDF):
- Week 1: finalize SLA band and pricing (this thread)
- Week 2: legal & procurement receive SOW + redlines
- Week 3: signature and SOC2 evidence exchange
- Week 4: onboarding kickoff

Two asks: 1) Are you sensitive to regional failover hours (we can include EU failover as a separate add-on), and 2) procurement contact for DocuSign delivery.

Attaching: redwood-proposed-sla-skus-20280306.pdf (summary matrix), SOC2-comparison-stub.xlsx (evidence).

Cheers,
Diego Fernández
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-proposed-sla-skus-20280306.pdf (application/pdf); SOC2-comparison-stub.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing tilt and negotiation posture (SignalOps)

Diego / Ben — quick notes before we send the detailed one-pager:

- SignalOps is medium-sized but growth-y; offering a 12–15% uplift on Preferred for a 36m commit is reasonable. Push for annual prepay to protect economics.
- For Assured (99.99%), price aggressively on retainer but limit credits to a sliding scale (0.5% per 30m of downtime). Avoid unlimited credits.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of retainer for 36m deals.
- Keep EU failover as an unbundled add-on — they'll likely push for included, we can trade for a higher commit.

Draft language I recommend for procurement (short):
- "Vendor agrees to service levels per Appendix A. For incidents breaching uptime bands, service credits capped at X% of monthly retainer, not exceeding Y% per quarter."

If you want, I can draft the procurement-friendly clause and the SOW appendix by EOD.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Pricing & Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Ari Glass <ari@signalops.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalOps Procurement <procurement@signalops.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA construct & pricing ask (SignalOps)

Diego — thanks for the fast turnaround and the SKU matrix. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and platform: 

- We like the Preferred package for day-to-day but want the Assured uptime band for a subset of traffic (payment-processing endpoints). Can you provide a blended quote: 80% Preferred / 20% Assured with a 36m commit?
- Procurement asks that onboarding credit be explicit on the SOW and that service credit caps be tabled (they dislike uncapped remediation credits).
- Can you confirm whether 24x7 Assured includes named escalation contacts and a 15-minute conference bridge within the P1 ack window — that is a hard requirement for our compliance team.

We can move fast if you send the blended quote + a procurement-friendly appendix. I'll route DocuSign as soon as legal signs off.
